title: legal redlines scratchpad - customer MSA review
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for negotiation talking points and clauses to watch when redlining customer MSAs / SOWs. Mostly shorthand and things to raise with sales/solutions.

Top priorities (quick):
- Cap on liability: push for single-digit % of fees (12 month lookback) OR fixed dollar cap tied to fees paid in prior 12 months. customer asking for unlimited / gross negligence carveouts -- reject.
- Indemnity: carve out third-party claims for IP infringement; limit to where customer uses models in accordance with docs. Avoid open-ended indemnity for customer outputs.
- Data use / model training: explicitly prohibit customer data from being used to train models unless paid/opt-in. Add clause: "Customer Data will not be used to improve or train models without explicit written consent."
- Confidentiality: standard 3-year period post-termination for business/confidential info; consider perpetual for trade secrets.
- Security & breach notification: 72 hour initial notice + remediation plan. Customer requests 24hrs -- negotiate to 72hrs unless PII exposure confirmed.
- SLA / uptime: customer wants 99.99% for hosted API. Our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% for Free/Dev tier; for enterprise can consider 99.95% with credits. Define credit matrix and exclude scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- Service credits: cap credits at monthly fee, not % of yearly revenue. Make credits sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures.
- Termination for convenience: customer asks for monthly termination; evaluate revenue exposure. For Dedicated/Private deals require 90-180 day notice + wind-down fees.
- Transition assistance: propose 60 days of limited transition support paid at standard SOW rates.
- Audit / compliance: customers want audit rights. Limit to vendor-provided reports (SOC2 type 2) + 1 remote audit per year with scope and redaction protections; on-site audits require reasonable notice and cost recovery.
- Subprocessors / third parties: require notice and ability to object for sensitive subprocessors. For cloud infra providers list allowed subprocessors in schedule.
- Data localization / export controls: if customer requires on-prem / VPC, move to Private deployment and add SOW for infrastructure costs.
- IP ownership: we own models, weights, improvements. Customer owns their input data and outputs produced for them (maybe license back to us for debug/ops?). Clarify limited license back to Redwood for debugging/quality improvements, excluding training.
- Warranty: disclaimers for model outputs ("as-is", no warranties regarding accuracy, suitability). For regulated use cases push to carve outs: customer must warrant appropriate use.
- Limitation of liability carveouts: ensure exclusions for confidentiality, willful misconduct remain so caps don't swallow everything.
- RMF / compliance templates: include SOC2 attestation + encryption details (data at rest, in transit), KMS options for Private.
- Evolving model performance / regressions: customer asks for performance guarantees; avoid specific model accuracy SLAs. Instead offer remediation: rollback to prior model and credits for measurable availability/perf regressions tied to pre-defined evals.

Negotiation talking points (to hand to AE):
- Data training: simple line: "We will not use Customer Data to train models without explicit written consent and commercially agreed terms." This is our redline non-starter for most customers.
- Liability: "Our aggregate liability capped at the greater of $X or fees paid in 12 months." Explain rationale: predictability for both sides.
- SLA expectations: "We can offer 99.95% with enterprise commitment + dedicated capacity; hosted accounts default 99.9%. Credits are capped at monthly fees and are sole remedy."
- IP / outputs: "Customer owns outputs. Redwood retains rights to improve and operate the service; any use of Customer Data for model improvement requires explicit opt-in."
- Audit asks: "We provide SOC2 reports and specific security evidence; on-site audits are exceptional and billable."

Redline hotspots in current MSA draft (section references approximate):
- Section 4.2 (Use of Data): customer language allows training -- redline to ban training without consent.
- Section 6.1 (Indemnity): broadened to include "claims arising from outputs" -- add intent/lawful use qualifier.
- Section 7 (Limitation of Liability): customer seeks removal; propose mutual limitation and carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- Section 9 (Termination): customer wants 30 day termination for convenience. For Dedicated deals escalate to 90/180 day and fees.
- Schedule B (SLA): missing exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure; add clear credit calc.

Open questions/need follow-up:
- Pricing impact if customer insists on no-data-training: do we need premium? Talk to pricing/SRE.
- Customer requires 24h breach notice for all incidents -- route to security to confirm acceptable language.
- Any regulatory geography requirements? If EU data residency, move to Private or Dedicated options.
- Is customer asking to host model weights? If yes, confirm license scope and redistribution restrictions.

Quick tactical redlines (phrases to add/change):
- "Customer Data" definition: explicitly include inputs, outputs, metadata; carve out aggregated/anonymous telemetry (we can retain for ops but not training).
- "Training" definition: include any model tuning, fine-tuning, reweighting, or use in algorithmic updates.
- "Sole and exclusive remedy": for SLA breaches credits only, no additional damages.
- "Force Majeure": include epidemics, cloud provider outages, and network failures; define notice obligations.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Loop in Solutions Eng for technical feasibility of requested performance guarantees.
- Pull precedent language from "enterprise-mas-template-v3" (Confluence) for indemnity and audit.
- For large strategic customers, be open to limited model-training carveouts with additional compensation and strict opt-out controls.

End of scratchpad.

(Informal: keep this doc short and messy -- will convert to formal redline template for Legal library after next negotiation.)
